subject: CobaltCart: Benchmark signoff packet & acceptance checkpoints
messages:

Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial load targets + quick ask before onboarding

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We're ready to proceed with the formal onboarding benchmark so we can sign off on production rollout. Before we lock in windows, can you confirm the acceptance criteria you plan to validate as part of the load runs? Specifically:

- Target p50 and p95 latencies for our chat flows (avg message length ~40 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target (RPS) and burst tolerance
- Any gating thresholds (error rate, tail latency) that would block go-live

We want to make sure our legal/finance teams see the same numbers in the signoff packet.

Also attaching the PO placeholder so procurement can start the paperwork once we agree on scope.

Attachment: po-cobaltcart-20270725.pdf (pdf stub)

Best,
Samir

CobaltCart
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@cobaltcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial load targets + quick ask before onboarding

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the PO stub. High level plan below; we can lock numbers once we see a short warmup run with your representative traffic.

Summary of proposed acceptance checkpoints (we'll produce a signoff packet with raw CSVs + dashboards):

- Latency: p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 250ms for 40-token messages on the recommended model variant; p99 target <= 750ms but not a hard blocker except under burst.
- Throughput: Sustained 120 RPS (requests/sec) with 10% headroom for sustained bursts; burst tolerance 300 RPS for up to 2 minutes with degraded p95 allowed.
- Error rate: <0.5% client-visible error rate during steady-state; any sustained 5xx >1% during a run will fail the gate.
- Tail/backpressure: KV cache warm-up expected for first 30s; we won't consider early warmup tail as a failure if artifacts are captured.

Proposed test window: Wed 2027-07-28 22:00 - 23:30 PDT (low-production overlap); we can shift to Thu if you need more prep time.

Attachments we will produce after the run: cobaltcart-benchmark-results.csv, slo-matrix-cobaltcart.pdf, and a readout doc with per-route traces.

Next steps: confirm the window and the traffic shape (QPS ramp profile + representative prompt set). I'll have Dev share the test harness instructions and an ephemeral API key for the run.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Jul 26, 2027 at 08:34 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of proposed acceptance checkpoints...

Thanks Logan — adding a few engineering specifics so your infra team can validate ahead of time:

Engine/test assumptions
- Model variant: rdx-13b-q4_traffic (recommended by inference team for throughput/quality tradeoff)
- Sequence length profile: 80% 20–60 tokens, 20% 60–200 tokens — we'll ask you to run both short and long prompt slices.
- Batching: tests will use continuous batching with max batch size 64; please notify if you want to restrict batch sizes for baseline runs.

Measurable acceptance thresholds (per-route):
- Chat (short): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms, throughput sustain 140 RPS.
- Chat (long): p50 <= 110ms, p95 <= 420ms, throughput sustain 60 RPS.
- Cold-start behaviour: first 3 minutes may show elevated tail latency due to kernel warm-up; we will exclude minute 0–3 from steady-state SLA calculations but will capture it in the packet.
- Error class: Any 5xx from our side or timeouts from your client >1% for longer than 5 minutes = fail.

Test plan highlights
- Ramp profile: 0 → 20% (2m) → 50% (4m) → steady for 20m → step to burst (2m) → cool-down.
- Jitter + realistic think-times will be applied to avoid synthetic uniform traffic.
- We'll collect per-token cost estimates and token-level latency breakdown for the packet.

Please confirm the exact prompt set you want us to use (we can consume your canonical 200 prompts or use our representative set).

Attachment: none on this email (we'll push results artifacts after the run).

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@cobaltcart.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Test harness + ephemeral keys

Samir — sending the short checklist for tomorrow's run:

1) We'll provision an ephemeral API key scoped to the benchmark project; that key will be rotated after the run.
2) Test harness (attached) contains the ramp profile, prompt set, and the script to reproduce runs locally. Please don't proxy through your load balancer — point the harness at the Redwood benchmark endpoint we provide.
3) If you use a client-side retry policy, set max retries=1 and backoff >= 200ms to avoid masking server-side errors.
4) If you want KV caching off for an isolated baseline, tell us and we'll flip it.

Attachment: benchmark-harness-instructions.txt (text stub)

I'll post the ephemeral key to the secure channel 30 minutes before the start.

Thanks,
Dev Patel

Thanks,

Samir / team — thanks for confirming. Quick clarifications and immediate next steps:

- The sustained 120 RPS we quoted is accepted requests measured at our ingress (retries are de-duplicated on the client side for billing). We'll include a clarified definition in the SLO matrix.
- Back-of-envelope cost: based on the model profile and the projected token mix, operating at the steady-state we discussed is approximately $12k–$16k/month. We'll produce a more granular per-token estimate in the signoff packet.
- We'll run the test as scheduled tonight; post-run you will receive: cobaltcart-benchmark-results.csv, slo-matrix-cobaltcart.pdf, and a drive folder with dashboards (link below).

Signoff conditions (what we'll need from CobaltCart):
1) Confirmation that PO placeholder can be converted to a committed order after signoff.
2) A brief email from legal approving the data retention/processing notes in the signoff packet.

Drive link to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CobaltCartBenchmark

If all looks good post-run we'll schedule a 30-minute readout with the CFO and engineering lead to approve the go-live.

Best,
